title: IndiGo Signs MoU With Ministry of Tourism to Promote Incredible India
excerpt: India's largest airline partners with the government's flagship tourism initiative as the ministry accelerates corporate tie-ups with airlines, tech companies, and content platforms to modernise the Incredible India brand.
body:
• IndiGo has signed a Memorandum of Understanding with India's Ministry of Tourism to jointly promote the Incredible India campaign across its network
  • The MoU follows similar partnerships the ministry has struck with Air India, Google India, and Netflix in recent months as part of a broader push to revamp India's tourism brand
  • With a fleet of over 400 aircraft serving 130-plus destinations, IndiGo gives the ministry access to one of the world's fastest-growing airline networks

IndiGo, India's largest airline by market share, has signed a Memorandum of Understanding with the Ministry of Tourism to jointly promote the government's flagship Incredible India campaign. The agreement was formalised in the presence of Union Tourism Minister Gajendra Singh Shekhawat and Neetan Chopra, IndiGo's Chief Digital and Information Officer, according to the airline.

Under the collaboration — branded #IncredibleIndiaByIndiGo — the two parties will work to showcase India's diverse landscapes, heritage sites, cultural traditions, and experiential tourism offerings to travellers both domestically and internationally. IndiGo said the partnership aims to strengthen India's position as a "world-class tourism destination" while "bringing more of the world closer to every corner of India."

A Pattern of Strategic Partnerships

The IndiGo deal is the latest in a series of corporate partnerships the ministry has struck in rapid succession this year. In late July, Air India signed its own MoU with the ministry to extend Incredible India branding across its global touchpoints, including co-branded marketing campaigns, inflight experiences, and trade engagement activities across key international markets.

"As the airline that proudly carries India in its name, Air India has a unique responsibility to showcase the country to the world and serve as an ambassador for the new India that is confident, vibrant, warm, and welcoming."

— Nipun Aggarwal, Chief Commercial Officer, Air India

In June, the ministry formalised its first comprehensive partnership with a global technology company, signing an MoU with Google India to integrate AI-powered travel demand insights, Google Maps for destination discovery, and YouTube optimisation for the Incredible India channel. The ministry has also partnered with Netflix to produce ten short promotional films showcasing Indian destinations, the first of which were unveiled at ITB Berlin earlier this year.

Why It Matters for India's Tourism Ambitions

The flurry of partnerships reflects a fundamental shift in how India markets itself to the world. The original Incredible India campaign, created in 2002 by then-bureaucrat Amitabh Kant and advertising agency Ogilvy & Mather, is widely credited with giving the country its first coherent tourism identity. Foreign tourist arrivals grew from 2.38 million that year to a peak of 10.93 million in 2019.

But the campaign's impact faded as global tourism marketing moved decisively toward digital platforms. The ministry's total allocation for 2026-27 stands at just ₹2,438 crore — a figure that Kant, who now sits on the boards of IndiGo, L&T, ITC, and HCL Tech, has publicly argued should rise to ₹20,000 crore to keep pace with competing destinations.

By leveraging corporate partners' distribution networks rather than expanding its own budget, the ministry is effectively outsourcing reach. IndiGo alone operates over 2,100 daily flights with a fleet of more than 400 aircraft, covering 90-plus domestic and 40-plus international destinations. That network gives the Incredible India message access to millions of passengers who might otherwise never encounter it.

Additional Secretary and Director General of Tourism Suman Billa has described the strategy as a "reboot" of Incredible India, emphasising AI, destination storytelling, and strategic partnerships. At the BOTT Knowledge Conclave earlier this year, Billa called for a unified "One India" approach and said AI-driven customisation is now essential for reaching modern travellers.

The Diaspora Connection

For India's overseas diaspora community, the deepening airline-ministry partnerships could have practical benefits. IndiGo has aggressively expanded its international footprint in recent years, launching direct services to destinations including Athens, London Heathrow, and Doha, while maintaining codeshare agreements with carriers such as Turkish Airlines, British Airways, Qantas, and American Airlines. Combined with Air India's presence across five continents, the dual partnerships create multiple touchpoints for NRIs and PIOs to discover — or rediscover — India's tourism offerings on routes they already fly.

What's Next

The ministry has signalled that more partnerships are in the pipeline. Its revamped Incredible India Digital Platform already integrates AI-powered personalisation, real-time weather updates, and OTA booking links. The next phase is expected to bring region-specific content targeting high-potential source markets, greater use of influencer and creator-led campaigns, and deeper collaboration with state tourism boards.

IndiGo, meanwhile, is entering a leadership transition. The airline's board has appointed former IATA chief William Walsh as its new CEO, with his tenure expected to begin in early August. How that transition shapes IndiGo's approach to strategic collaborations beyond aviation — including nation-branding — will be closely watched by the industry.
